title: Capacity Lifecycle PRD: tenant surge controls, soft-reserves, and autoscale orchestration
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Summary:

This PRD defines a unified approach to capacity lifecycle management for Redwood Dedicated: soft-reserve allocations, tenant surge (burst) protection, and autoscale orchestration across reserved pools. The goal is to reduce noisy-neighbor incidents, provide predictable SLOs for reserved customers, and enable safe transient burst behavior without manual operator intervention.

Background:

Customers on Dedicated want predictable latency and throughput for reserved workloads while retaining the ability to absorb short-lived spikes (bursts). Current behavior allows uncontrolled burst that can saturate shared nodes or cause eviction cascades. We need explicit lifecycle rules: soft-reserve (minimum standby capacity that can be temporarily borrowed), preemptible burst tokens, and coordinated autoscale policies that respect tenant isolation and cross-tenant fairness.

Goals:
- Define API and control-plane primitives for soft-reserves and burst tokens tied to reservations.
- Implement autoscale orchestration that triggers scale-up/down events with tenant-aware prioritization and graceful preemption policies.
- Surface operational controls in Console: per-reservation SLA, burst window config, and eviction policy selection.
- Protect best-effort tenants from sustained noisy neighbors while allowing short exponential backoff style bursts.

Non-goals:
- Rewriting the serving runtime. This PRD focuses on orchestration, policy, and control plane features; low-level kernel optimizations remain separate.
- Cross-region migration mechanisms.

User stories and personas:
- As a Platform Engineer (enterprise customer), I want my reserved pool to guarantee 95th percentile latency under normal load, and be able to accept bursts up to 2x for 60s without losing state.
- As an SRE at Redwood, I want automatic graceful preemption that avoids mass eviction and gives engineers clear telemetry when tenants are throttled.
- As a Product Manager, I want a single Console page to configure soft-reserve values, burst policies (window, multiplier, cooldown), and to see historical burst events.

Requirements (high level):
1) Control-plane primitives: reservation object extension to include soft_reserve_percent, burst_window_seconds, burst_multiplier, cooldown_seconds.
2) Autoscale orchestration: a coordinator service that evaluates pool utilization and issues scale events or rebalances requests across pools based on policy.
3) Preemption semantics: preemption must be staged with graceful drain: notify in-flight requests, mark new requests as best-effort, evict only when drain threshold exceeded.
4) Observable signals: per-tenant metrics for bursts (count, duration), preemption events, queue length, latency by token tier; Console alerts + audit log entries for policy changes.
5) Backwards compatibility: existing reservations without new fields should default to conservative soft_reserve=10%, burst_multiplier=1.25, window=30s.

Acceptance criteria:
- The control plane accepts and persists new reservation fields and exposes them in the Console UI.
- Autoscale coordinator can perform a simulated scale-up scale-down in staging using tenant-aware prioritization with no request loss in 95% of test scenarios.
- When a tenant exceeds burst limits, the system enforces cooldown and preemption rules; there is a recorded audit event and per-tenant metrics show the action within 1 minute.
- Operator can set a global fallback policy that routes overflow to pre-warmed best-effort pools or to hosted API fallback with documented latency implications.
- E2E canary rollout plan tested: start with internal customers (redwood-dev), then progressive roll to small set of paying customers, with automatic rollback on SLO regressions.

Design trade-offs considered:
- Aggressive vs conservative soft-reserve defaults: aggressive increases utilization but risks SLO violations; default chosen conservative (10%) to prioritize latency.
- Immediate eviction vs staged preemption: staged chosen to reduce error spike and debugging complexity.
- Coordinator centralization vs decentralized decision making: centralized orchestration simplifies cross-tenant fairness but is a single point to scale horizontally; we will implement as a horizontally scalable leader-elected service.

Monitoring & SLOs:
- New SLO: Reserved-95 latency must not regress >10% post-rollout for any reserved tenant.
- Alerting: add alert when >5% of reserved tenants enter preemption within a 10m window.
- Dashboards: per-pool utilization, burst events heatmap, preemption timeline.

Rollout plan:
1) Implement control plane schema changes and Console surfaces behind feature flag.
2) Implement autoscale coordinator in staging; run synthetic load tests with chaos injection.
3) Canary with 3 internal reserved pools for 48h.
4) Expand to 5 customers for 2 weeks with monitoring and operational runbook.
5) General availability and documentation.

Operational playbook (high level):
- If mass preemption occurs, toggle feature flag to disable coordinator, fail open to conservative autoscale, and engage oncall to triage tenant causing sustained burst.
- For customer support: provide per-tenant burst report (CSV) and recommended reservation changes.

Open questions:
- Should burst tokens be billable differently or considered free within short windows? (billing input needed)
- Exact cooldown calculus for sequential bursts (linear vs exponential backoff).
- Do we support cross-pool borrowing across different GPU families? (depends on compatibility matrix)
acceptance_criteria: Control plane accepts/persists new reservation fields and shows in Console
Autoscale coordinator performs scale actions in staging with <5% request loss in test scenarios
Preemption enforcement logs audit events within 1 minute and updates per-tenant metrics
Global fallback routing is configurable and documented with latency trade-offs
Canary rollout completed and no SLO regressions observed for reserved tenants
decisions: Default soft_reserve_percent = 10% to prioritize SLOs over utilization
Implement staged preemption (notify -> drain -> evict) to reduce error spikes
Coordinator will be a horizontally scalable leader-elected service to balance fairness and availability
